enrichment.headline: Adopts a plan to lay off classified staff for 2022-23 if funds or work run short
enrichment.summary: The Board is adopting a resolution that allows the district to reduce classified (non-teaching) staff for the 2022-23 fiscal year because of a lack of funds or a lack of work. The text does not say how many positions are affected or name specific jobs.

pulled.summary: Adopted in its own vote at this meeting (5–2), instead of with the rest of the consent report.

items.title: Classified Employees Reduction In Force - Lack of Funds and/or Lack of Work - 2022-2023 Fiscal Year - Talent/Human Resources Department

enrichment.headline: Freezes hiring for school site and central office positions starting January 27, 2022
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving a temporary hiring freeze that covers positions at school sites and in the central office. The freeze takes effect January 27, 2022. The text does not say when it ends.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Temporary Hiring Freeze – School Sites and Central Office Positions – Talent/Human Resources Department

enrichment.headline: Ratifies up to $2,500 for English classes for parents at East Oakland Pride Elementary
enrichment.summary: The Board is ratifying (approving after the fact) a services agreement with an Oakland contractor to teach English as a Second Language (ESL) classes to 25-30 parents, twice a week for 16 weeks, at East Oakland Pride Elementary School. The agreement runs January 24 to March 25, 2022, and began before the Board's vote. Payment is capped at $2,500, from Title I grant funds.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Emma Donnelly - East Oakland Pride Elementary School

enrichment.headline: Subcontracts up to $400,000 of child development funding to The Unity Council
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving a subcontract that passes a portion of the district's 2021-22 child development funding, up to $400,000, to the Spanish Speaking Unity Council of Alameda County (The Unity Council) for general child care and development programs. The period runs July 1, 2021 to June 30, 2022, so it began before the Board's vote.

vendor.name: Spanish Speaking Unity Council of Alameda County, Inc. (The Unity Council)

items.fundingSource: General Child Development Program CCTR Grant

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Subcontract - Spanish Speaking Unity Council of Alameda County, Inc. - General Child Care and Development Programs - Early Childhood Education

enrichment.headline: Subcontracts up to $200,000 of child development funding to the YMCA of the East Bay
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving a subcontract that passes a portion of the district's 2021-22 child development funding, up to $200,000, to the YMCA of the East Bay for general child care and development programs. The period runs October 1, 2021 to June 30, 2022, so it began before the Board's vote.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Subcontract - YMCA of the East Bay - General Child Care and Development Programs - Early Childhood Education

enrichment.headline: Pays Spearitwurx up to $97,500 for equity and wellness sessions for school staff
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving a services agreement with Spearitwurx for equity and wellness work through the Office of Equity: a staff assessment, school site visits, 5-7 customized sessions (15 hours of facilitation), wellness kits, and coaching for selected staff. The agreement runs January 3 to June 30, 2022, so it began before the Board's vote. Payment is capped at $97,500.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Spearitwurx - Office of Equity

enrichment.headline: Approves Castlemont High trip to tour Oregon colleges and volunteer, at no cost to the district
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving an out-of-state trip for 12 Castlemont High School students and 3 adults to Eugene, Oregon, from January 31 to February 4, 2022. The group will volunteer with Habitat for Humanity and tour Bushnell University, Lane Community College and the University of Oregon. The trip costs the district nothing.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Student Travel - College and University Campuses Tour - Eugene, Oregon - Castlemont High School

enrichment.headline: Allows district boards to meet virtually in February 2022 under the Brown Act
enrichment.summary: The Board is adopting a resolution making the findings needed to let district public bodies hold virtual meetings in February 2022. The Brown Act is California's open-meeting law for public bodies.

pulled.summary: Adopted in its own vote at this meeting (4–3), instead of with the rest of the consent report.

items.title: District "Brown Act" Legislative Bodies - February 2022 - Virtual Meetings - Board of Education

enrichment.headline: Finds charter schools cannot be accommodated at a single site, with written reasons
enrichment.summary: The Board is adopting a resolution that finds charter schools cannot be accommodated at a single site and sets out a written statement of reasons for that finding. The title ties it to school year 2022-23. The text itself does not give the reasons.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Charter Schools Facilities Request - Finding/Reasons - Charter Schools Could Not Be Accommodated - Single Site - School Year 2022-2023 - Charter Schools Office

enrichment.headline: Leases the Ascend Campus to Ascend Charter School for two years, about $216,367 in 2022-23
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving a two-year facilities use agreement, July 1, 2022 to June 30, 2024, letting Ascend Charter School use the 44,704-square-foot Ascend Campus. The charter school pays a Proposition 39 per-square-foot rate in 2022-23 and 1.05 times that year's rate in 2023-24. The district expects about $216,367 in revenue in 2022-23.

pulled.summary: Adopted in its own vote at this meeting (5–2), instead of with the rest of the consent report.

items.title: In-Lieu of Proposition 39 Facilities Use Agreement for 2022-2024 - Ascend Charter School - Office of Charter Schools

enrichment.headline: Leases 2111 International Blvd to Community School for Creative Education, about $126,351 in 2022-23
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving a one-year facilities use agreement, July 1, 2022 to June 30, 2023, with an option to extend through June 30, 2024, for the charter school to use 2111 International Blvd. Rent is set by Proposition 39 per-square-foot rates: 17,870 square feet at the base rate and 3,994 square feet at two times the rate. The district expects about $126,351 in revenue in 2022-23 (if elected).

pulled.summary: Adopted in its own vote at this meeting (5–2), instead of with the rest of the consent report.

items.title: In-Lieu of Proposition 39 Facilities Use Agreement for 2022-2023, With Option for 2023-2024 - Community School for Creative Education - Office of Charter Schools

enrichment.headline: Leases the Toler Heights Campus to Francophone Charter School, about $35,922 in 2022-23
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving a two-year facilities use agreement, July 1, 2022 to June 30, 2024, letting Francophone Charter School use the 7,422-square-foot Toler Heights Campus. The charter school pays a Proposition 39 per-square-foot rate in 2022-23 and 1.05 times that year's rate in 2023-24. The district expects about $35,922 in revenue in 2022-23 and may adjust the fee based on districtwide maintenance and operations costs.

pulled.summary: Adopted in its own vote at this meeting (5–2), instead of with the rest of the consent report.

items.title: In-Lieu of Proposition 39 Facilities Use Agreement for 2022-2024 - Francophone Charter School - Office of Charter Schools

enrichment.headline: Leases the Tilden Campus to Urban Montessori Charter School, about $157,431 in 2022-23
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving a two-year facilities use agreement, July 1, 2022 to June 30, 2024, letting Urban Montessori Charter School use the 32,527-square-foot Tilden Campus. The charter school pays a Proposition 39 per-square-foot rate in 2022-23 and 1.05 times that year's rate in 2023-24. The district expects about $157,431 in revenue in 2022-23.

pulled.summary: Adopted in its own vote at this meeting (5–2), instead of with the rest of the consent report.

items.title: In-Lieu of Proposition 39 Facilities Use Agreement for 2022-2024 - Urban Montessori Charter School - Office of Charter Schools
